# ParallelLingvo — full context

ParallelLingvo is a multilingual vocabulary learning application. The central product idea is "one word, every language you speak": a single vocabulary concept stays connected to every language a learner selects, instead of duplicating that concept across separate bilingual decks.

## Product purpose

Designed for multilingual learners, international families, immigrants, students preparing for language exams, international professionals, travelers, and anyone who studies or uses several languages at the same time.

## Core idea and hero pitch

"One word. Every language you speak." Most vocabulary apps make learners rebuild the same word list for every language pair. ParallelLingvo keeps one concept — with all its translations, example sentences and pronunciation — in a single card. A learner studies a word once and moves forward in every language they've selected at the same time.

## How the practice exercise works

Each card shows the word's translations across the learner's active languages. One language is the current "target": its word is hidden and the learner spells it out letter by letter by dragging or tapping tiles into place, rather than simply recognising a printed answer. Getting it right reveals the sentence and unlocks pronunciation audio (spoken via text-to-speech, one voice per language). A learner can flag a word as difficult to review it separately later, and a daily-goal timer tracks study time per session.

## Main capabilities

- AI-built lessons: give it a word, a list, or a topic; it produces translations, example sentences and a ready lesson.
- Learning you can guide: parent accounts assign lessons, set a priority topic, and see each child's real progress.
- One concept, all languages: a single concept links to several languages at once rather than separate language-pair decks.
- Connect via MCP: add words directly from any AI tool already in use, through an MCP connector.
- Focus on difficult words: mark tricky words and train them in a separate, focused review.

## Four ways to fill a deck (word sources)

1. Upload your own list — paste words; AI translates them into the target languages and writes an example sentence for each.
2. Let AI generate words — pick a topic and a level (A2/B1/B2); AI builds a whole deck from scratch.
3. Connect another AI — add words through an MCP connector from any AI tool already in use (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini).
4. Get a deck from a friend — another user can share their deck directly via a share code or username.

## Family accounts

A parent account and a child account share one deck and stay in sync:
- Real progress, not guesses — words learned, streak and accuracy per language, updated live.
- Priority lessons — the parent picks which topic the child practices first.
- Synced word lists — the parent's and child's decks are always the same set.
- Hand over new words — words a parent adds land directly in the child's queue.

## Language catalog

48 languages at launch: the major European languages plus Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian and Vietnamese. The catalog can grow without redesigning the underlying data model, since vocabulary concepts are stored independently of any specific language column.

## Platforms

- Telegram Mini App — https://app.parallellingvo.app/
- Web app (mobile-first) — https://app.parallellingvo.app/
- Android app — https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.parallellingvo
- iOS — planned, not yet available.

## Pricing

- Free, with ads — €0/month: 48 languages, unlimited lessons, audio and difficult-word review; no AI-built lessons.
- €3/month, no ads — everything in Free, ad-free experience.
- €6/month, best value — everything in the €3 plan, plus AI-built lessons and AI-generated translations and example sentences.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Which languages are supported?
A: 48 at launch: the major European languages plus Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian and Vietnamese. More can be added without redesigning storage.

Q: Can I really learn more than three languages at once?
A: Yes. Translations stay attached to the same concept, so a session in one lesson moves every selected language forward.

Q: How is it different from a flashcard app?
A: Flashcards are bilingual by design — one deck per pair. Here the structure itself is multilingual, and you type the word out letter by letter instead of just recognising it.

Q: Does it work on mobile?
A: Yes — a mobile-first web app, an Android app, and a Telegram mini app. Native iOS is planned.

This is a separate concern from the 48-language learning catalog above — the marketing site's translation set is expanded independently from the languages the application teaches.
